Ravi: proposal: fragment-based warmstart for safetensors. exporter emits a sidecar manifest (.frag.json) with stable fragment ids, offsets, lengths, and optional group_hint so runtimes can hydrate minimal ranges.
Maya: nice. how do we coordinate ownership when many nodes try to hotplug the same fragment?
Ravi: use a weak-lease registry (not full RAFT). leases are short-lived TTLs persisted to control-plane DB. semantics: lease grant -> node streams fragment -> node atomically publishes READY. if lease expires or node dies, lease holder is invalidated and another node can acquire.
Jenna: what about in-progress partial pages on crash? we need a tombstone/rollback marker so readers don't observe half-hydrated fragments.
Ravi: agree. runtime state machine: TO_FETCH -> STREAMING -> COMMIT -> READY. on crash, coordinator marks fragment as ORPHAN and a reconcilier job either rolls back partial pages or resumes streaming. tombstones are small records in DB.
Kellen: kernel compatibility: some fused ops need whole tensors. add model-variant tags at export time so runtime can decide merge vs fallback. exporter should emit a single-shard fallback variant if fragmentation used.
Ravi: example fragment manifest snippet: ```json
{"version":"1","fragments":[{"id":"f0","off":0,"len":2097152,"group_hint":"g0"},{"id":"f1","off":2097152,"len":2097152,"group_hint":"g0"}],"variants":["sharded","single_shard_fallback"]}```
Maya: perf: small fragments increase parallel reads but hurt syscalls. group_hint lets transport coalesce adjacent fragments into a single range read. telemetry should report fragment_hydration_ms and coalesce_hit_rate.
ci-bot: canary deploy scheduled: frag-warmup-handler v0.1 -> tonight 02:30 UTC :rocket:
Ravi: plan: PoC (manifest + local partial reads) -> canary lease registry -> full GC/reconciliation path. I'll open a short RFC with failure modes and test vectors.
